messages:
Avery (Eng Manager): Quick one — we just discovered a former contractor (now FT) received a promotion mid-cycle but approvals were delayed. They already signed a manager offer verbally. What are the rules for retro pay, tax gross-ups, and whether we can backdate to the verbal acceptance date?
Priya (People Ops): Oof. Short: verbal offers are risky. Official effective_date must be backed by paperwork and approvals. Retro pay can be applied to the effective_date once approvals are final, but we cant backdate before employment start or convert contractor invoices to salary. If verbal acceptance predates paperwork, we still need signed docs + committee approvals to set retro.
Avery (Eng Manager): They accepted verbally 2026-03-10, started FT 2026-03-18, manager duties began 2026-03-22. I want effective_date = 2026-03-10. Any legal exposure?
Helen (Legal): Legal here: we avoid retroactive employment terms before start date. You can request an effective_date earlier than start only in narrow cases; legal review required. Also be careful about creating implied contracts based on verbal offers. Please submit a legal memo if you want earlier effective_date.
Sasha (Compensation): For level change >10% or band crossing we need comp committee sign-off. Retro pay to cover manager duties is allowed but taxed in the period it's paid. Tax gross-up for retention or sign-on? Those are discretionary and need Finance/Legal sign-off; not typical. Attach market comp and manager justification.
Omar (Payroll): Practical limits: payroll cutoff is 4 business days before US pay date. If approvals land after cutoff we can do off-cycle or next-run retro. Off-cycle triggers processing fees and requires Finance OK. Also payroll cannot reissue contractor invoices as salary; contractor period stays as contractor pay.
Avery (Eng Manager): Understood. What docs do I need to file right now to maximize chance of retro to 03-10?
Priya (People Ops): Submit leveling packet + comp-change form, attach signed offer (even if signed now), manager justification noting scope/duties and dates, written confirmation from the hiring vendor that contractor invoices ended, and a short legal memo requesting earlier effective_date. Mark `expedite=true` and note retention risk.
Avery (Eng Manager): I'll upload signed offer and vendor termination today.
PeopleOpsBot: Leveling packet URL: https://redwood.company/hr/leveling_packet. Set fields: effective_date, retro_request=true, expedite_reason, headcount=conversion. For comp >10% set needs_comp_committee=true.
Sasha (Compensation): Also flag whether you want a one-time discretionary payment to cover gap vs base retro. Finance prefers one-time discretionary payments over changing historical contractor pay. If you request discretionary gap payment, include justification and cost code.
Avery (Eng Manager): Preference is base retro to 03-10 for manager pay. If committee declines, I'll consider discretionary payment.
Helen (Legal): We'll need the legal memo ASAP explaining why earlier effective_date is justified. Consider risk of creating precedent. We'll advise on wording for manager communication if approved.
Omar (Payroll): FYI, if retro spans multiple tax years we need to coordinate tax reporting. Also state/local withholding might change; payroll will include detail line items on the paystub.
Priya (People Ops): Note about gross-ups: Payroll + Finance will only approve gross-ups in exceptional retention or relocation cases and Legal must sign off. Its not standard for promotions. If you want gross-up, include a strong business case.
Avery (Eng Manager): Uploaded docs and vendor termination. Submitted leveling packet and set expedite.
Sasha (Compensation): Received. Routing to leveling committee now. If leveling approves, comp committee will evaluate the >10% increase and retro request. Expect 1-3 business days.
Helen (Legal): I've got the memo. Quick read: recommending effective_date = 2026-03-18 (start date) rather than verbal acceptance. If you still want 03-10 explain exceptional business need.
Avery (Eng Manager): Retention risk is high; candidate had other offer. I added that to expedite reason.
Sasha (Compensation): Leveling committee approved the manager mapping but flagged the retro_request for comp committee.
Omar (Payroll): Watch the cutoff: next payroll run cutoff is 2026-03-29. If comp approval arrives after that, retro will be next-run adjustment unless Finance approves off-cycle.
Sasha (Compensation): Comp committee approved base retro to 2026-03-10 on a one-off with Finance agreement, but only if Legal signs off on precedent memo. They also approved pro-rated manager equity.
Helen (Legal): Given the retention risk and documentation, Legal approves the one-off earlier effective_date for this case only. We'll add a note to the employee file about precedent limits.
Priya (People Ops): Great. Omar, can payroll process retro to 03-10 including base difference? Finance will cover any off-cycle fees?
Omar (Payroll): We can process retro to 03-10. Finance needs to confirm off-cycle fee coverage if it requires manual processing; if it fits into next run, no extra fee. Please confirm desired payout timing (next regular run or off-cycle).
Avery (Eng Manager): Next regular run is fine if thats simpler.
Sasha (Compensation): Finance team please confirm.
Priya (People Ops): Finance confirmed they will absorb off-cycle fee for this retention case. Omar, schedule for next regular run with retro adjustment to 03-10 if cutoff allows; otherwise include as next-run adjustment.
Omar (Payroll): Copy. I'll prepare feed and ensure payslip lines show retro and tax breakdown.
Avery (Eng Manager): Thanks all. One last Q: what do we tell the employee now?
Helen (Legal): Tell them: "promotion approved with paperwork processing; effective date set to 2026-03-10 pending final payroll processing; official letter forthcoming." Keep wording careful about verbal acceptance.
Priya (People Ops): We'll generate the official comp letter and manager email template. Closing thread after payroll confirmation. :white_check_mark:
